mainTopic: ארץ ישראל and the sources of rain; when to start asking for rain; fasting when rain is late
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer from the previous daf: a פסוק about gathered sea water describes creation, not how rain works today. A ברייתא then lists four ways ארץ ישראל is special in creation and rainfall, and illustrates the last of them with a משל of a cheese-maker. The גמרא goes back to רבי אליעזר's claim that ocean water is sweetened in the clouds and proves it from the one-letter difference between חשכת and חשרת. It then explains how רבי יהושע reads those same פסוקים, and which side a ברייתא about the upper waters follows. Next come אגדות about water and size: the world drinks from the runoff of גן עדן, a chain of sizes ends with the world being like a lid over גיהנם, and בבל is praised for being rich because of its rivers. A new משנה gives the date for starting to ask for rain. The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל (the 7th of מרחשון) in ארץ ישראל, and follows חנניה (sixty days into the תקופה) in the גולה, with day sixty itself counting as 'after'. A second משנה teaches the stages of fasting when rain is late. The גמרא explains that the יחידים who fast first are the רבנן and that they fast Monday, Thursday, Monday, and it brings a supporting ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: That verse is about the creation of the world
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of an answer from the previous daf: a verse describing sea water gathered in one place refers to the time of creation, not to how the world is watered today.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is speaking about the creation of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of an answer that began on the previous daf. A verse about gathering the sea water is explained as describing the world's creation, not how rain works now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, a פסוק about sea water (כונס כנד מי הים) seemed to support the view that the world drinks from the ocean. The answer limits that פסוק to the beginning of creation, when all the water was gathered in the deep. That way it no longer proves anything about how rain works today.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It finishes an answer that started on the previous daf. Read it as the end of that discussion, not the start of the next one.

phrases.english: [That verse refers] to the creation of the world.
phrases.notes: Completes the answer begun on 9b. The verse describes the original state of the waters at creation.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּבְרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to a challenge from the previous daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the verse to a different time period (the time of creation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse about gathered sea water describes how the world is watered now.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse describes only the original creation, so it proves nothing about present-day rainfall.

steps.title: ארץ ישראל was created first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that ארץ ישראל was created before the rest of the world, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: ארץ ישראל was created first, and the whole rest of the world was created afterward. As it says: 'While He had not yet made the land and the outside places.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the special status of ארץ ישראל. Its first point is that ארץ ישראל was created before the rest of the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names 'ארץ' first and 'חוצות' second. The ברייתא reads 'ארץ' as ארץ ישראל, the main land, and 'חוצות' as the lands outside it. The order of the words in the פסוק shows the order of creation.

keyTerms.meaning: The outside places, meaning lands outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The Land of Israel was created first,
and the entire rest of the world was created afterward,
as it says: 'While He had not yet made the land and the outside places.'
phrases.notes: משלי ח:כו. 'Land' means ארץ ישראל. 'Outside places' means the other lands.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל נִבְרֵאת תְּחִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא, connected to the earlier topic of how the world receives water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ארץ ישראל was created before the rest of the world, learned from the order of 'ארץ' and 'חוצות' in the פסוק.

steps.title: God waters ארץ ישראל Himself
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: הקדוש ברוך הוא waters ארץ ישראל directly, while the rest of the world is watered through a messenger.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself waters ארץ ישראל, and the whole rest of the world is watered through a messenger. As it says: 'Who gives rain upon the land, and sends water upon the outside places.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second point in the ברייתא. ארץ ישראל gets its rain directly from הקדוש ברוך הוא, while other lands get theirs through a שליח (messenger).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the two verbs in the פסוק. 'הנותן' (He gives) describes direct, personal giving to the 'ארץ.' 'ושולח' (and sends) describes sending something through someone else to the 'חוצות.'

phrases.english: The Land of Israel is watered
by the Holy One, Blessed be He, Himself,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ עַל יְדֵי שָׁלִיחַ,
phrases.english: and the entire rest of the world through a messenger,
as it says: 'Who gives rain upon the land,'
'and sends water upon the outside places.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַשְׁקֶה אוֹתָהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the second special quality of ארץ ישראל in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ארץ ישראל is watered directly by הקדוש ברוך הוא, and the rest of the world through a שליח.

steps.title: ארץ ישראל gets real rain; the world gets the leftovers
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: ארץ ישראל drinks actual rainwater, while the rest of the world drinks the leftover residue.
steps.simpleTranslation: ארץ ישראל drinks rainwater, and the whole rest of the world drinks from the residue. As it says: 'Who gives rain upon the land,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third point in the ברייתא. ארץ ישראל receives the actual rain, and the rest of the world gets what remains in the clouds afterward (תמצית).
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same פסוק but focuses on a different detail. The 'ארץ' gets 'מטר,' real rain. The 'חוצות' only get 'מים' sent afterward, which is what is left over.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Etc.', meaning the rest of the פסוק

phrases.english: The Land of Israel drinks rainwater,
and the entire rest of the world [drinks] from the residue,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הַנֹּתֵן מָטָר עַל פְּנֵי אָרֶץ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: as it says: 'Who gives rain upon the land, etc.'
phrases.notes: The same פסוק as before, now read for what each place receives.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שׁוֹתָה מֵי גְשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק to derive a third quality.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ארץ ישראל receives real rain, and the rest of the world receives the leftover residue.

steps.title: ארץ ישראל drinks first, like a cheese-maker taking the good part
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's final point: ארץ ישראל is watered first and the world afterward, illustrated by a משל of someone making cheese who takes the good food and leaves the waste.
steps.simpleTranslation: ארץ ישראל drinks first, and the whole rest of the world afterward. As it says: 'Who gives rain upon the land,' and so on. This is like a person kneading cheese: he takes the food and leaves the waste.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the fourth and last point in the ברייתא. The timing is also special: ארץ ישראל is watered first, and a משל explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions the 'ארץ' before the 'חוצות,' showing the order of watering. In the משל, a cheese-maker first takes the good curds and only leaves the leftover liquid behind. In the same way, ארץ ישראל gets the best and first share, and the rest of the world gets what comes after.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא lists four special qualities of ארץ ישראל: (1) created first, (2) watered directly by הקדוש ברוך הוא, (3) gets real rain rather than residue, (4) is watered first. Each one is learned from פסוקים that contrast 'ארץ' (ארץ ישראל) with 'חוצות' (the other lands), through word order, the verbs 'נותן' and 'שולח', or what each place receives.

phrases.english: The Land of Israel drinks first,
and the entire rest of the world afterward,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הַנֹּתֵן מָטָר עַל פְּנֵי אָרֶץ וְגוֹ׳״ —
phrases.english: as it says: 'Who gives rain upon the land, etc.'
A parable: a person who kneads cheese

phrases.aramaic: נוֹטֵל אֶת הָאוֹכֵל וּמַנִּיחַ אֶת הַפְּסוֹלֶת.
phrases.english: takes the food and leaves the refuse.
phrases.notes: The best goes first to ארץ ישראל, and what remains goes to the rest of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שׁוֹתָה תְּחִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא with a fourth quality and a משל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ארץ ישראל is watered first and the rest of the world afterward, like taking the good part and leaving the waste.

steps.title: What is the source that ocean water is sweetened in the clouds?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to an earlier statement, that salty sea water becomes sweet in the clouds, and asks where we learn this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'They are sweetened in the clouds.' From where does he know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line from earlier in the discussion, that ocean water is sweetened in the clouds. It asks for the source, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר held that the world drinks from ocean water. When asked how, since ocean water is salty, he answered that it becomes sweet in the clouds. Now the גמרא wants a פסוק that supports this claim.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said', quoting an earlier statement in order to discuss it
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: The Master said:
'They are sweetened in the clouds.'
phrases.notes: Referring to the salty ocean waters, per רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: From where does he derive this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מִמַּתְּקִין הֵן בְּעָבִים. מְנָלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא and goes back to the earlier discussion about ocean water.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source for the claim that ocean water becomes sweet in the clouds.

steps.title: Two nearly identical verses hint at sweetening in the clouds
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף, quoting רבי יוחנן, points to two parallel פסוקים, one saying 'חשכת מים' and the other 'חשרת מים.' The difference between them becomes the source (explained next).
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: it is written, 'Darkness of waters, thick clouds of the skies,' and it is written, 'Gathering of waters, thick clouds of the skies.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting רבי יוחנן, who points out that two almost identical פסוקים differ by a single letter. Step 8 explains how this proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תהלים says 'חשכת' (darkness) and שמואל ב says 'חשרת' (gathering). Only one letter is different. רבי יוחנן reads meaning into the switch between them, and that reading will show that the clouds turn dark, salty water into fresh rain.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not finished here. These two פסוקים are just being set side by side. The next lines explain how the one-letter difference shows that water is sweetened in the clouds.

phrases.english: As Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
It is written: 'Darkness of waters, thick clouds of the skies,'
and it is written: 'Gathering of waters, thick clouds of the skies.'
phrases.notes: שמואל ב כב:יב. Only one letter differs from the first פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 by bringing scriptural sources.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the comparison of two parallel פסוקים, 'חשכת מים' and 'חשרת מים.' Step 8 explains how they prove the point.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא learns from tiny wording differences between parallel פסוקים in different books of תנ״ך.

steps.title: Combining the two spellings to read 'making fit'
steps.stepSummary: Take the כ from 'חשכת' and the ר from 'חשרת' to form 'חכשרת', which means the water is made fit, or sweetened, in the clouds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Take the כ, put it together with the ר, and read the word as 'חכשרת', which means 'making fit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from step 7. It merges the two spellings into one new word that proves the clouds make sea water drinkable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק says 'חשכת מים' and the parallel פסוק says 'חשרת מים.' Put the letters of both words together (ח-כ-ש-ר-ת) and you get 'חכשרת', meaning 'making fit.' So the פסוק hints that in the clouds the salty water is made fit to drink, which supports רבי אליעזר's view that rain comes from the ocean.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the textual source for the idea, raised earlier, that salty ocean water turns sweet in the clouds.

phrases.english: Take the kaf and place it with the reish
phrases.notes: The כ comes from חשכת and the ר from חשרת.

phrases.english: and read into it 'chakhsharat' (rendering fit).
phrases.notes: The water is 'made fit' in the clouds.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁקוֹל כָּף וּשְׁדִי אַרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 7 by explaining what the one-letter difference teaches.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Merging חשכת and חשרת produces חכשרת, showing that water is made fit (sweetened) in the clouds.

steps.title: How does רבי יהושע read these פסוקים?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע does not hold that rain comes from the ocean, so what does he learn from these two פסוקים?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע: what does he learn from these פסוקים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the other side, רבי יהושע, explains the same two פסוקים. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע holds that rain comes from the upper waters, not from the ocean. So he does not need a source that clouds sweeten sea water. The גמרא wants to know what lesson he takes from the חשכת/חשרת difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he expound from them?

steps.confusionAlert: This is רבי יהושע from the earlier מחלוקת with רבי אליעזר. He is not the same person as רבי יהושע בן לוי, who appears later here.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua, regarding these verses,
what does he expound from them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, בְּהָנֵי קְרָאֵי מַאי דָּרֵישׁ בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי אליעזר's reading to ask how the opposing view uses the same פסוקים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יהושע learns from the חשכת/חשרת פסוקים.

steps.title: Dark clouds hold much water
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע agrees with the saying from ארץ ישראל that bright clouds hold little water and dark clouds hold a lot.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like what רב דימי said when he came from ארץ ישראל. They say in the West: bright clouds have little water, dark clouds have much water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהושע uses the פסוקים to teach a fact about clouds: dark clouds carry more water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'חשכת' means darkness and 'חשרת' means a gathering. רבי יהושע reads the two פסוקים together: where the clouds are dark, a lot of water is gathered. So he still learns something from the פסוקים, just not the sweetening of sea water.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who brought teachings from ארץ ישראל to בבל

phrases.english: He holds in accordance with this,
that when Rav Dimi came, he said:
They say in the West (Eretz Yisrael):
Bright clouds have little water.
Dark clouds have much water.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כִּי הָא דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע reads 'darkness of water' together with 'gathering of water' to mean that dark clouds hold much water.

steps.title: Whose view matches the ברייתא about the upper waters?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the upper waters hang by ה׳'s word and their 'fruit' is rain. Which opinion does it follow?
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view matches what was taught: the upper waters hang by ה׳'s word, and their fruit is rainwater, as it says, 'The earth is satisfied from the fruit of Your works'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא and asks which side of the מחלוקת it fits. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says rainwater is the 'fruit' of the upper waters. That ties rain to the waters above. The גמרא wants to identify which תנא holds this.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper waters, above the sky

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that which was taught:
The upper waters are suspended by the word (of God),
and their fruit is rainwater,
as it is stated: 'From the fruit of Your works the earth is satisfied.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא into the רבי אליעזר / רבי יהושע מחלוקת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the ברייתא about the upper waters follows.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא matches רבי יהושע, who holds that rain comes from the upper waters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view? רבי יהושע's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא fits רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If rain is the 'fruit' of the upper waters, then rain comes from above. That is exactly רבי יהושע's position.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? With Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן — כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11.

steps.title: How רבי אליעזר reads that פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says the פסוק 'From the fruit of Your works' speaks about ה׳'s handiwork in general, not about the upper waters.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר? That פסוק is written about the work of ה׳'s hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי אליעזר is not contradicted by the פסוק, because he reads it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used the פסוק to say rain is the 'fruit' of the upper waters. רבי אליעזר answers that 'Your works' means ה׳'s handiwork in general. So the פסוק does not prove that rain comes from above, and his view stands.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer? That verse

phrases.aramaic: בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: regarding the handiwork of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is what it is written about.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: הָהוּא, בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הוּא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the other side avoids the proof that the ברייתא's פסוק seemed to give.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר reads the פסוק as referring to ה׳'s handiwork, not to the upper waters.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע have a way to read each set of פסוקים. רבי אליעזר: rain is ocean water made fit in the clouds. רבי יהושע: rain comes from the upper waters.

steps.title: The whole world drinks from גן עדן's runoff
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that the whole world is watered by the leftover water of גן עדן, based on 'A river went out of Eden.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: the entire world drinks from the runoff of גן עדן, as it says, 'And a river went out of Eden.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins: the water of the whole world is only the overflow of גן עדן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a river went out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it split into rivers that watered the world. So the world gets only what is left over after גן עדן is watered. This continues the earlier theme that ארץ ישראל is watered first and the world gets the residue.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע בן לוי is an אמורא. He is not the same person as the תנא רבי יהושע discussed just before.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The entire world
drinks from the runoff of the Garden of Eden,
as it is stated: 'And a river went out of Eden, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ מִתַּמְצִית גַּן עֵדֶן הוּא שׁוֹתֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new statement on the theme of where the world's water comes from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole world is watered by the runoff of גן עדן.

steps.title: A measurement for runoff
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the runoff of a field the size of a בית כור can water a field the size of a תרקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: from the runoff of a בית כור, a תרקב's area can be watered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a measurement. It sets up a size comparison between גן עדן and the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תרקב-field is one sixtieth of a בית כור-field. If runoff waters an area one sixtieth the size of its source, and the world drinks from גן עדן's runoff, then the world is one sixtieth the size of גן עדן.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A field large enough to plant a כור of seed
A field for half a סאה of seed, 1/60 of a בית כור

phrases.english: It was taught: From the runoff of a beit kor
a tarkav's area is watered.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: מִתַּמְצִית בֵּית כּוֹר שׁוֹתֶה תַּרְקַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a measurement to רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement, setting up a size comparison.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Runoff waters an area one sixtieth the size of its source.
steps.whyThisMatters: Combined with step 14, this implies that the world is one sixtieth the size of גן עדן.

steps.title: The world compared to the size of גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives a chain of sizes. Each place is one-sixtieth of the next one, until the whole world is like a pot lid on top of גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: The land of מצרים is 400 פרסה by 400 פרסה. It is one-sixtieth of כוש. כוש is one-sixtieth of the world. The world is one-sixtieth of the גן. The גן is one-sixtieth of עדן. עדן is one-sixtieth of גיהנם. So the whole world is like a pot cover for גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that continues the theme of גן עדן from the last step. It builds a ladder of sizes, each one sixty times bigger than the one before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step said the runoff of a big field waters a small one. This ברייתא goes further and shows how huge גן עדן and עדן are compared to our world. At the very end it shows that even עדן is tiny next to גיהנם, so our whole world is just a 'lid' on top of it.

keyTerms.meaning: A large land south of מצרים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'the Garden' (גן) and 'עדן'. They are two different places here. The גן is the garden, and עדן is a much bigger place that the garden sits inside. The river flowed out of עדן to water the גן.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם הָוְיָא אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת פַּרְסָה
phrases.english: The land of Egypt is four hundred parsa
by four hundred parsa,
and it is one-sixtieth of Cush,
and Cush is one-sixtieth of the world,
and the world is one-sixtieth of the Garden,
and the Garden is one-sixtieth of Eden,
and Eden is one-sixtieth of Gehinnom,
it turns out that the entire world
is like a pot cover for Gehinnom.
phrases.notes: The world sits over גיהנם like a small lid on a huge pot.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם הָוְיָא אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת פַּרְסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the theme of גן עדן watering the world by showing the relative sizes of the world, the גן, עדן, and גיהנם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each region is one-sixtieth of the next. The whole world is like a pot cover over גיהנם.

steps.title: Other opinions: גיהנם or עדן has no measure
steps.stepSummary: Two other views. One says גיהנם has no measure at all. Another says עדן has no measure at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: גיהנם has no measure. And some say: עדן has no measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds two other opinions that disagree with the exact size chain we just saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion gave every place a fixed size. These views say that one of the places is endless. One view says גיהנם has no limit, and the other says עדן has no limit.

keyTerms.meaning: It has no measure, no limit
Eden, the place the river flows out of

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: גֵּיהִנָּם אֵין לָהּ שִׁיעוּר,
phrases.english: And some say: Gehinnom has no measure,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: עֵדֶן אֵין לָהּ שִׁיעוּר.
phrases.english: and some say: Eden has no measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: גֵּיהִנָּם אֵין לָהּ שִׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers other opinions instead of the measured chain of sizes in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to these other opinions, either גיהנם or עדן is without limit.

steps.title: בבל's storehouses are full because of its waters
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא explains the פסוק about בבל. Its storehouses are full of grain because it sits on many waters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: What is the meaning of what is written: 'You who dwell on many waters, abundant in storehouses'? What caused בבל to have storehouses full of grain? You must say: because it dwells on many waters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new water topic. רבי אושעיא explains a פסוק in ירמיהו about בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links two things: 'many waters' and 'many storehouses.' רבי אושעיא says the first causes the second. בבל's rivers, the חידקל and the פרת, water its fields, so it always has plenty of grain.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written (introduces a פסוק to explain)
You must say, it must be

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said: What is the meaning of what is written:
'You who dwell on many waters, abundant in storehouses' (Jeremiah 51:13),
what caused Babylonia
to have its storehouses full of grain?
You must say:
because it dwells on many waters.
phrases.notes: Its rivers make the land easy to water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the cosmic sizes of places to the water source of one specific land, בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בבל is rich in grain because it is watered by many rivers.

steps.title: בבל harvests even without rain
steps.stepSummary: רב says בבל is wealthy because it can harvest crops even without rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: בבל is wealthy, for it harvests even without rain.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a similar idea in support of רבי אושעיא. בבל does not depend on rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא linked בבל's grain to its rivers. רב spells out what this means in practice. Because the rivers water the fields, בבל gets a harvest even in a year with no rain.

phrases.english: Rav said: Babylonia is wealthy,
for it harvests without rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: עַתִּירָה בָּבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אושעיא with a parallel statement about בבל's independence from rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בבל gets harvests even without rain.

steps.title: A swampy land is better than a dry one
steps.stepSummary: אביי says we have a tradition: a soggy, swampy land is better than a dry land.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We hold: swampy, and not dry.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי closes the section on בבל with a short rule. Land full of water is better than dry land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This puts the praise of בבל into a general principle. Wet, swampy land like בבל keeps producing crops. Dry land depends on rain and can fail.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold, we have a tradition

steps.whatToRemember: בבל is wealthy because its rivers water it. It does not need rain, so wet land is better than dry land.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We hold:
swampy and not dry (is better).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: נְקִיטִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the praise of בבל into a general rule about land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A swampy land is better than a dry land.

steps.title: When do we start asking for rain?
steps.stepSummary: New משנה. The תנא קמא says we start asking for rain on the 3rd of מרחשון. רבן גמליאל says the 7th, fifteen days after the חג, so the last pilgrim can reach the נהר פרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: On the third of מרחשון we ask for rain. רבן גמליאל says: on the seventh of it, fifteen days after the חג, so that the last Jew can reach the נהר פרת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It moves from mentioning rain to actually asking for rain in שמונה עשרה, and gives two opinions about the date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned when we 'mention' rain (משיב הרוח). Now the question is when we 'ask' for rain (ותן טל ומטר). We wait after סוכות so the pilgrims who came to ירושלים can travel home on dry roads. רבן גמליאל adds four more days, until the 7th, which is fifteen days after the חג, so that even the farthest pilgrim, who lives by the נהר פרת, gets home before the rain.

keyTerms.meaning: We ask for rain (in ברכת השנים)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Asking' for rain (שאלה, ותן טל ומטר) is different from 'mentioning' rain (הזכרה, משיב הרוח). Mentioning starts on שמיני עצרת. Asking starts later.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: On the third of Marcheshvan
we ask for rain.
Rabban Gamliel says: on the seventh of it,
fifteen days after the Festival.
phrases.notes: Counted from the end of the חג (שמיני עצרת, the 22nd of תשרי).

phrases.english: so that the last of the Jewish people can reach
the Euphrates River.
phrases.notes: The last pilgrim on his way home from ירושלים.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה בִּמְרַחְשְׁוָן שׁוֹאֲלִין אֶת הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה about the date for asking for rain, after the אגדה about water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says we ask for rain from the 3rd of מרחשון. רבן גמליאל says from the 7th, so pilgrims can reach the פרת first.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל: we start asking for rain on the 7th of מרחשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי אלעזר said: The הלכה is like רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by deciding the מחלוקת in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of the two dates in the משנה, the 3rd and the 7th, רבי אלעזר picks the 7th. In ארץ ישראל we start asking for rain on the 7th of מרחשון.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא (start of the discussion on the משנה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is still the practice in ארץ ישראל today. ותן טל ומטר starts on the 7th of חשון.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Elazar said:
The halacha is like Rabban Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the מחלוקת in the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In ארץ ישראל we begin asking for rain on the 7th of מרחשון.

steps.title: In the גולה, wait sixty days into the תקופה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes חנניה: in the גולה, we do not start asking for rain until sixty days into the autumn season (תקופת תשרי).
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: חנניה says: And in the גולה, until sixty days into the תקופה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a ברייתא about a different place, the גולה, which has its own date for asking for rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's dates are for ארץ ישראל. חנניה says that in the גולה (בבל) we wait longer, until sixty days after the start of תקופת תשרי, the autumn equinox. This fits what we just learned: בבל is full of water and does not need rain as early.

keyTerms.meaning: Season. Here, תקופת תשרי, starting at the autumn equinox

phrases.english: It was taught: Chananya says:
And in the Diaspora, until sixty days into the season.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, חֲנַנְיָה אוֹמֵר: וּבַגּוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a separate rule for the גולה beside the rule for ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the גולה we begin asking for rain sixty days after the start of תקופת תשרי.

steps.title: The הלכה follows חנניה for the גולה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל, quoted by רב הונא בר חייא, rules that the הלכה follows חנניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חייא said that שמואל said: The הלכה is like חנניה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the halacha for the גולה, just as it did for ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So there are two set rules. In ארץ ישראל we ask from the 7th of מרחשון, like רבן גמליאל. In the גולה we ask from sixty days into the season, like חנניה.
steps.whatToRemember: Two dates for ותן טל ומטר: the 7th of מרחשון in ארץ ישראל, and sixty days after תקופת תשרי in the גולה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice outside ארץ ישראל of starting ותן טל ומטר in early December (around December 4th or 5th).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chiya said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is like Chananya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כַּחֲנַנְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules that the הלכה follows חנניה's opinion from Step 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the גולה, we begin asking for rain sixty days after the start of תקופת תשרי.

steps.title: שמואל seems to give a different date for asking for rain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling that שמואל follows חנניה, because שמואל was quoted giving a different sign: we start asking for rain when wood is brought into the house of טבות the bird hunter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But they asked שמואל: From when do we mention 'and give dew and rain'? He told them: From when they bring wood into the house of טבות the bird hunter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ruling from step 24. If שמואל holds like חנניה (sixty days), why did he give a completely different sign?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24, שמואל ruled like חנניה: start asking for rain sixty days into תקופת תשרי. Here שמואל is quoted saying something that sounds different: start when people bring firewood into a certain man's house. That looks like a contradiction in שמואל's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? An opening word that signals a challenge
But look! It introduces a contradicting source
'And give dew and rain', the request for rain added in the weekday עמידה
Bird hunter, the job of the man named טבות

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But they asked Shmuel:
From when do we mention 'and give dew and rain'?
He said to them: From when they bring in wood
phrases.notes: People bring firewood indoors once the cold, rainy season sets in.

phrases.english: to the house of Tavut the bird hunter!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מִשְּׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 24 using another statement of שמואל
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the הלכה follows חנניה (sixty days into תקופת תשרי)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל elsewhere gave a different marker (wood brought into טבות's house), which seems to contradict a sixty-day count.

steps.title: Both signs point to the same time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two statements are the same: wood was brought into טבות's house at exactly the sixty-day point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps this one and that one are one and the same measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. Both of שמואל's statements describe the same moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל was not giving a new date. He was giving a practical, real-life sign that fell on the same day as sixty days after תקופת תשרי. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, both of them
A measure, an amount of time

phrases.english: Perhaps this one and that one
are one measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי חַד שִׁיעוּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: two descriptions of the same time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's wood sign was a different date from sixty days, contradicting his ruling like חנניה
steps.terutzMaskana: The wood sign is just a practical marker of the sixty-day point, so שמואל is consistent

steps.title: Does the sixtieth day count before or after?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether day sixty itself belongs to the period before the sixty days or to the period after.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is the sixtieth day treated like before sixty, or like after sixty?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about counting. On day sixty itself, do we already start asking for rain or not yet?
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנניה said we wait sixty days. That leaves day sixty itself unclear. If it counts as 'before', we start on day sixty-one. If it counts as 'after', we start on day sixty itself.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them, a real open question

phrases.english: It was asked of them: The sixtieth day,
is it like before sixty or like after sixty?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: יוֹם שִׁשִּׁים, כְּלִפְנֵי שִׁשִּׁים אוֹ כִּלְאַחַר שִׁשִּׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new detail question about חנניה's sixty-day rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the sixtieth day itself is part of the waiting period or the start of asking for rain

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about day sixty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a dispute: רב says day sixty counts as after, and שמואל says it counts as before.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב said, the sixtieth day is like after sixty. שמואל said, the sixtieth day is like before sixty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that רב and שמואל already argued about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, we start asking for rain on day sixty. According to שמואל, day sixty is still part of the waiting time, so we start the next day. The answer does not settle the question yet; it shows there are two views.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, introducing a source that answers

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: יוֹם שִׁשִּׁים כִּלְאַחַר שִׁשִּׁים,
phrases.english: Rav said: The sixtieth day is like after sixty,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: יוֹם שִׁשִּׁים כְּלִפְנֵי שִׁשִּׁים.
phrases.english: and Shmuel said: The sixtieth day is like before sixty.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, רַב אָמַר: יוֹם שִׁשִּׁים כִּלְאַחַר שִׁשִּׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27 by citing a dispute
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a dispute: רב says after (start on day sixty), שמואל says before (start on day sixty-one)

steps.title: A memory aid: those above need water
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a way to remember who said what: people up high need water, people down low do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Your memory sign is: those above need water, those below do not need water.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a memory trick so we don't mix up the opinions of רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water flows downhill, so low places get water easily and high places need rain more. רב learned in ארץ ישראל, which is high, so he starts asking earlier (day sixty). שמואל lived in low-lying בבל, so he starts later (after day sixty).

keyTerms.meaning: Those above, people living in high places
Those below, people living in low places

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
And your sign: those above need water,
those below do not need water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: וְסִימָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a memory aid for the dispute in step 28
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one from the higher land (רב) starts asking for rain earlier; the one from the lower land (שמואל) starts later

steps.title: The הלכה: day sixty counts as after
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules like רב: day sixty counts as after, so we start asking for rain on day sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The הלכה is that the sixtieth day is like after sixty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא settles the dispute and rules like רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because day sixty counts as after the waiting period, people in the גולה begin asking for rain on day sixty itself.
steps.whatToRemember: In the גולה we start asking for rain sixty days after תקופת תשרי, and day sixty itself is included (like רב).
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the source for the practice outside ארץ ישראל of starting 'ותן טל ומטר' around early December.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The halakha is:
The sixtieth day is like after sixty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute of step 28
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב: we start asking for rain on the sixtieth day.

steps.title: No rain by the 17th of מרחשון: individuals fast
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if no rain has fallen by the 17th of מרחשון, individuals start three fasts. These are light fasts: eating at night is allowed, and work, bathing, oil, shoes and marital relations are all permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the 17th of מרחשון arrived and no rain fell, the individuals begin fasting three fasts. They eat and drink after dark, and they are permitted in work, bathing, anointing with oil, wearing shoes, and marital relations.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches the first stage of fasting when rain is late: only special individuals fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 17th of מרחשון is ten days after the 7th, when we start asking for rain. If rain still hasn't come, select individuals fast three fasts. These fasts are mild: they start in the morning, and only eating and drinking are forbidden during the day.

keyTerms.meaning: Individuals, here outstanding people (not the whole community)
After it gets dark, the night before the fast

steps.confusionAlert: 'Eat and drink after dark' means the night before the fast day. The fast starts in the morning, unlike יום כיפור, which starts the evening before.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If the seventeenth of Marcheshvan arrived
and rain did not fall —
the individuals begin to fast three fasts.
They eat and drink after dark,
and they are permitted in work and in bathing
and in anointing with oil and in wearing shoes
and in marital relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הִגִּיעַ שִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר בְּמַרְחֶשְׁוָן וְלֹא יָרְדוּ גְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about fasting when rain is delayed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the 17th of מרחשון without rain, individuals fast three mild fasts that begin in the morning.

steps.title: No rain by ראש חודש כסלו: the community fasts
steps.stepSummary: If still no rain has fallen by ראש חודש כסלו, the בית דין decrees three fasts on the whole community, with the same mild rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: If ראש חודש כסלו arrived and no rain fell, the בית דין decrees three fasts on the community. They eat and drink after dark, and they are permitted in work, bathing, anointing with oil, wearing shoes, and marital relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the second stage: now the whole community must fast, by order of the בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step up here is who fasts, not how strict the fast is. Before, only individuals fasted; now the בית דין requires everyone. The rules stay the same: only eating and drinking during the day are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day of the month כסלו

steps.whatToRemember: Late rain leads to stages of fasting: first individuals (17 מרחשון), then the whole community (ראש חודש כסלו). So far, both stages have the same mild fast rules.

phrases.english: If the New Moon of Kislev arrived
and rain did not fall —
the court decrees
three fasts on the community.
They eat and drink after dark,
and they are permitted in work and in bathing
and in anointing with oil and in wearing shoes
and in marital relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִגִּיעַ רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ כִּסְלֵיו וְלֹא יָרְדוּ גְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the next, broader stage of fasting
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From ראש חודש כסלו without rain, the בית דין decrees three mild fasts on the entire community.

steps.title: Who are the individuals in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking who the יחידים mentioned in the משנה are.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who are the 'individuals'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section starts here. It asks a simple question about the word יחידים in the משנה, and this sets up רב הונא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that יחידים start fasting on the 17th of מרחשון, but it never said who they are. Is it any single person who wants to fast, or a specific group? The גמרא wants a definition.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion section that comes after the משנה
Individuals; here, special people who fast before the whole community does

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא's discussion.

phrases.english: Who are the 'individuals'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן ״יְחִידִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה quoted in step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the יחידים who fast first.

steps.title: רב הונא: the individuals are the Sages
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the יחידים are the רבנן, the Torah scholars.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: They are the רבנן (the Sages).
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. The 'individuals' are not just anyone. They are the Torah scholars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholars are held to a higher standard, so they are expected to fast early, before the whole community is asked to. 'Individuals' here therefore means a distinguished group, not random people.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a leading Babylonian scholar

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read יחידים as 'any private person who chooses to fast.' According to רב הונא, it refers specifically to the Sages.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The Sages (Torah scholars).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.

steps.title: רב הונא: the individuals fast Monday, Thursday, Monday
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא adds that the three fasts of the יחידים fall on Monday, Thursday, and the following Monday.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא also said: The individuals fast three fasts, on Monday, Thursday, and Monday.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a second teaching. He tells us which days of the week the individuals' three fasts fall on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said 'three fasts.' רב הונא sets the order: they start on a Monday, not on a Thursday. This becomes the subject of the challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: And Rav Huna said:
Individuals fast three fasts,
Monday, Thursday, and Monday.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר רַב הוּנָא: יְחִידִים מִתְעַנִּין שָׁלֹשׁ תַּעֲנִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement by the same אמורא, setting the schedule of the fasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יחידים' three fasts are on Monday, Thursday, and Monday.

steps.title: Challenge: we already know this order from a משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב הונא adds, since a משנה already teaches that the first three fasts are Monday, Thursday, Monday, and never start on a Thursday.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned in a משנה: We do not decree a fast on the community starting on a Thursday, so as not to drive up prices. Instead, the first three fasts are Monday, Thursday, and Monday!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא. His second teaching seems unnecessary, because a משנה already says this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A later משנה (15b) says community fasts never begin on a Thursday. If the first fast fell on Thursday, people would buy food for after the fast and for שבת at the same time. Shopkeepers would see the rush, think a famine was coming, and raise prices. Since the Monday-Thursday-Monday order is already taught there, what does רב הונא add?

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (that we did not already know)
We have already learned (in a משנה)

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned:
We do not decree a fast on the community
starting on a Thursday,
so as not to drive up prices,
rather, the first three fasts are
Monday, Thursday, and Monday!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָמַשְׁמַע לַן? תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's statement in step 35 as repeating what a משנה already teaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that the יחידים fast Monday, Thursday, Monday.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: a משנה already sets this order for fasts, so the statement seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Answer: the משנה spoke only about the community
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought the order applies only to a ציבור, so רב הונא teaches that it applies to a יחיד as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: this applies only to a community, but not to an individual. So he teaches us that it applies to individuals too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רב הונא's teaching is needed because the משנה only spoke about the community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the משנה's rule was the price rush that a public fast could cause. We might think a private group's fast does not affect the market, so it could start on any day. רב הונא teaches that individuals also follow the Monday-Thursday-Monday order.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)

phrases.english: You might have said:
this applies only to a community,
but not to an individual;
so he teaches us (that it does).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי צִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge of step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extending the rule: the משנה covers the ציבור, and רב הונא extends it to the יחיד.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Monday-Thursday-Monday order applies only to community fasts, so individuals could start on any day.
steps.terutzMaskana: Individuals also must fast Monday, Thursday, Monday.
steps.whatToRemember: The no-Thursday-start rule is not only for public fasts. The individual scholars who fast first also follow the Monday-Thursday-Monday order.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב הונא: when individuals begin fasting, they fast Monday, Thursday, Monday, and they stop for ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: When the individuals begin to fast, they fast Monday, Thursday, and Monday, and they interrupt the fasts for ראשי חדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רב הונא, which backs up his teaching. The ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states outright that individuals fast Monday, Thursday, Monday. This confirms רב הונא's point. It also adds a new detail: if a fast day falls on ראש חודש, the fasts are paused, because one does not fast on a festive day.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא), meaning a supporting source

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב הונא's teaching is not just his own opinion. It matches an earlier תנאי source.

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a baraita):
When the individuals began to fast,
they fast Monday, Thursday, and Monday,
and they interrupt (the fasts) for New Moons,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues past the end of this passage.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the conclusion of step 37 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that individuals fast Monday, Thursday, Monday.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that individuals fast Monday, Thursday, Monday and pause for ראש חודש.
